text:
liam: Drafting a small proposal — tiered burst credits with network-aware fallback for API-key admission. Idea: per-key token-buckets for steady qps + short burst credits that draw from org pool. If GPU queue depth or regional network congestion is high, route to cheaper model or place in short hold queue with retry hints. @sofia @jess any immediate concerns?
jess: sounds useful. how do you prevent one org from burning all burst credits across keys? :thinking:
liam: two layers — per-key bucket + org shared bucket. Keys can borrow from org bucket subject to a per-key cap and exponential backoff once org pool drained. also add decay to returned credits over time.
sofia: network-aware fallback — do you mean region-level signal (e.g., high p95 egress or lost packets)? need to avoid cross-region hops for private deploys.
liam: yeah region-level signals + node GPU queue depth. fallback policy example: prefer local cheaper variant (quantized model) -> if still saturated, queue with Retry-After header -> finally respond 429 when grace exhausted.
mike: implementation note: Admission proxy already has per-key token-bucket logic. We can add an org-level redis counter + leaky refill. worried about storm of redis writes during bursts.
anya: could we keep soft state in local proxy and sync occasionally to redis for long-lived changes? local fastpath uses in-memory counters for short bursts, fallback to redis if borrow needed.
liam: exactly. local in-proxy buckets for low-latency refills; org pool as redis-backed reservoir with CAS for borrows. add circuit for redis timeouts to avoid making admission depend on network.
infra-bot: metrics snapshot: region-us-west p95-gpu-queue=420ms, api-keys-burst: 12% of keys used >50% org-burst in last 5m.
jess: what about accounting & billing? bursts consumed should be billable and visible in console. we need audit logs for any redis CAS borrow.
liam: billing events emitted on confirmed charge (when borrow succeeds). for queued requests we emit events on enqueue/dequeue with sampling. logs include org_id,key_id,borrow_amount,reason.
mike: pseudo refill logic I sketched:
```
// per-key refill on request grant
key.tokens = min(key.capacity, key.tokens + elapsed * key.rate)
if key.tokens >= cost: allow
else if org.tokens >= cost && key.borrowable: atomically decrement org.tokens and grant
else enqueue short-hold with Retry-After
```
anya: enqueue should be bounded per-key to avoid head-of-line blocking; use per-key FIFO with max_hold=200ms then drop to 429.
sofia: for private deployments: add config toggle to disable cross-region fallback and prefer local queueing only. also expose network signal via edge probes to proxies.
jess: curious about fairness across org tiers (free vs paid). propose tier multiplier for org pool refill_rate and longer grace for paid.
liam: agree — refill_rate multiplier per plan + priority borrow weight. lower tiers get smaller borrow caps. default conservative so we don't regress latency for heavy users.
mike: storage debate: Redis hash vs separate keys per org. separate keys easier for TTL and atomic decrements. also use Lua script for borrow CAS.
liam: action items: 1) draft PR adding org-bucket support in admission proxy (mike), 2) design redis schemas + lua scripts (anya + mike), 3) add network signal probe + fallback config (sofia), 4) console metric+billing hooks (jess).
sofia: I'll add private-deploy safe mode config and doc.
jess: +1 to action items. :thumbsup:
liam: cool. i'll spin up a short design doc and link it here when ready. flagging for eng-infra planning board. :rocket:
